evidence: Cic. Fam. 7.18.1: significābant enim tē istam mīlitiam jam firmō animō ferre
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to show by signs; to show, point out, express, publish, make known, indicate”; with an accusative and infinitive when a letter or a sign shows that something is so. Of a word, “mean” (see mean).

terms.gloss: point out, be a sign of; reveal
evidence: Publil. Sent. I 43: Inertia indicātur, cum fugitur labor.
Publil. Sent. P 61: Parātae lacrimae īnsidiās, nōn flētum indicant.
terms.comment: First conjugation, with a short i; not indīcō, indīcere, proclaim.

terms.gloss: point out (as with a finger), show
evidence: Catull. 55.1–2: dēmōnstrēs ubi sint tuae tenebrae

phrases.latin: significābant enim tē istam mīlitiam jam firmō animō ferre et esse fortem virum et cōnstantem
phrases.english: for they showed that you are now bearing your military service with a steady mind, and are a brave and steadfast man

phrases.latin: Parātae lacrimae īnsidiās, nōn flētum indicant.
phrases.english: Tears at the ready indicate a trick, not grief.

sources: Lewis & Short: significo · Lewis & Short: indico · Lewis & Short: demonstro
